questions.question: How to login with Azure CLI?
questions.searchLine: [azure-cli • login • powershell • authentication • azure • azure-cli-login] How to login with Azure CLI?
questions.answerText: To login to Azure using Azure CLI and run PowerShell commands: powershell Connect-AzAccount -DeviceCode Get-AzSubscription Set-AzContext -Subscription "azure-practicing" Get-AzContext Get-AzVM -Status This will authenticate you to Azure and allow you to manage your Azure resources.
questions.answerHtml:
To login to Azure using Azure CLI and run PowerShell commands:

Connect-AzAccount -DeviceCode
Get-AzSubscription
Set-AzContext -Subscription "azure-practicing"
Get-AzContext
Get-AzVM -Status

This will authenticate you to Azure and allow you to manage your Azure resources.

questions.question: How to grant local Administrator rights centrally via GPO?
questions.searchLine: [gpo • group-policy • admin • rdp • windows • active-directory • azure • gpo-admin-rdp] How to grant local Administrator rights centrally via GPO?
questions.answerText: configure-admin-gpo.ps1 mirrors configure-rdp-gpo.ps1, but targets the local Administrators group (SID S-1-5-32-544) instead of Remote Desktop Users (SID S-1-5-32-555). Run it on the DC, then grant access domain-wide via one AD group instead of editing local groups per VM: powershell On the DC .\configure-admin-gpo.ps1 Add-ADGroupMember -Identity "Domain-Admins" -Members "username" ⚠️ Members of Domain-Admins get full local admin rights on every computer the GPO applies to (domain root by default) — scope the GPO link to a specific OU if that's too broad. To verify on the target VM: powershell gpupdate /force Get-LocalGroupMember -Group "Administrators" should list DOMAIN\Domain-Admins gpresult /r confirm "Allow Local Admin Access via Group Policy" is in Applied GPOs whoami /groups | findstr "Administrators" confirm the logged-in user has admin rights
questions.answerHtml:
configure-admin-gpo.ps1 mirrors configure-rdp-gpo.ps1, but targets the local Administrators group (SID S-1-5-32-544) instead of Remote Desktop Users (SID S-1-5-32-555). Run it on the DC, then grant access domain-wide via one AD group instead of editing local groups per VM:

# On the DC
.\configure-admin-gpo.ps1
Add-ADGroupMember -Identity "Domain-Admins" -Members "username"

⚠️ Members of Domain-Admins get full local admin rights on every computer the GPO applies to (domain root by default) — scope the GPO link to a specific OU if that's too broad.

To verify on the target VM:

gpupdate /force
Get-LocalGroupMember -Group "Administrators"   # should list DOMAIN\Domain-Admins
gpresult /r                                    # confirm "Allow Local Admin Access via Group Policy" is in Applied GPOs
whoami /groups | findstr "Administrators"      # confirm the logged-in user has admin rights
